items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: Mass was the director of the club and not the band leader... he told me that I was fired.

ctx.x: A few nights before I was to play in Brussels, some young fellows came to the club St. Germain and asked me if I could be engaged to play a few numbers on a river barge which they had transformed into a club. I told them they would have to get permission from Guy Masse and he gave it. The concert in Brussels was on a Sunday night and this thing on the barge was the following Monday night. I returned to Paris that Monday afternoon and played one set at the club St. Germain. Someone from the barge came to get me…

I waited around for quite a while, and after midnight came, I still had not played anything. I decided to take a taxi and go back to the club. When I arrived, Guy was furious because I had not come back in time to do the show. As he had given me permission to go to this gig, I didn't figure that he was expecting me back at a certain time. I finished the night at the club and he told me that I was fired. He just could speak a little English, and his words for telling me I was fired, were that he was kicking me…

Soon after I finished at the Club St. Germain, I received an offer to do two concerts in Berlin and left by train for Hannover the 27th of March. When I arrived in Hannover the 28th, I took a plane to Berlin. There I was met at the airport by some men from the television and two German jazz fans, Hans Blutner and Fritz Krull. They presented me to an American boxer named Tiger Jones who was campaigning in Germany.
